approach: Three parts inside the existing mechanical-revision flow, so no critic round is used. (1) admission.rs: `open_questions_findings` gets a third `else if` branch, after the no-addressee and says-the-code-answers branches. It gives a major finding at "open questions", even for a User:/Host: question, when the question asks (a) whether existing tests break (adjacent tokens existing|other + test|tests, or tests + outside, plus a break/fail word) or (b) what a backticked named function does on its failure or retry path. A decision word (should, may, prefer, want, expect, wish, allowed, acceptable) exempts a question. So does a host-environment word (host, toolchain, platform, machine, os), because the code cannot show those facts (critic finding 2). (2) planner.md: the new content goes into line 5 in place of '; name only files, functions and commands you saw'. The bytes come from merging line 9 (callers, `include_str!`, output assertions) into line 8 (dependents) and from trimming repeated wording. No enumeration is deleted: defaults.toml, all five commit shapes, the rule categories and the 'every rule is stated here' clause stay (critic findings 1 and 3). (3) Tests: admission.rs unit tests, refusal_corpus.rs cases, and a job_plan.rs test that drives the scripted planner/critic Scenario. planning.rs gets a comment only, and fake.rs stays unchanged on purpose.

decisions.choice: Put the rule in `open_questions_findings` as a third `else if` branch calling a new helper `asks_about_existing_behavior`. At most one finding per question. An unprefixed test-breakage question keeps the 'no addressee' finding.
decisions.reason: Existing tests count one finding per question (admission.rs:1179-1203; `question_findings` in refusal_corpus.rs:3277-3298 expects exactly one). The only production caller chain is plan_findings (admission.rs:314) <- planning.rs:217. Its major findings return `RoundEnd::Mechanical` before `critic_round`, so no critic round is used.

decisions.choice: Match words on the lowercased text, split on non-alphanumerics. Test-breakage: an adjacent pair (existing|other, test|tests) or (tests, outside), AND a token in {break, breaks, broken, breakage, fail, fails, failing, failure, failures, regress, regresses, regression}. Function: a backticked identifier (alphanumeric, `_`, `:`, optional trailing `()`; no space, `/` or `.`) AND one of 'what does', 'what happens', 'how does' AND one of 'failure path', 'retry path', 'on failure', 'on retry', 'on error', 'when it fails', 'if it fails'. Both predicates are skipped when the question has a decision token {should, may, prefer, want, expect, wish, allowed, acceptable} OR a host-environment token {host, toolchain, platform, machine, os}.
decisions.reason: Answers critic finding 2 (earlier round). 'Host: do existing tests fail on the production host's older toolchain?' asks a host fact the code cannot show, so the host-environment token exempts it by rule, not by luck of wording. The cost is a documented miss: a User: question that mentions a platform and asks about existing-test breakage is not refused, and the critic and the brief cover it. Paths such as `crates/athena-cli/tests/job_plan.rs` give the token 'tests' but never a pair with existing/other/outside, so the scope questions accepted at admission.rs:1225-1229 and refusal_corpus.rs:3265 still pass.

rejected.option: Pin the Host: toolchain question in the corpus as a known false positive
rejected.why: It would refuse a real host question, and a refused host question cannot be answered by the planner at all.

rejected.why: Refuses real decisions and scope questions (admission.rs:1226).

rejected.why: 'User: what does the user expect `athena land` to print?' is a decision, not a code fact.

risks.risk: The wording match refuses a genuine User: or Host: decision.
risks.mitigation: The rule is narrow: adjacent existing|other + test(s) (or tests + outside) with a break/fail word, or a backticked function name with a failure/retry phrase and 'what does/happens/how does'. A decision word or host-environment word exempts the question, and the counterexamples are pinned as accept cases in admission.rs and in the corpus. A refused planner rewords and loses one mechanical pass, not a critic round.

risks.risk: The check misses rewordings ('does the suite still pass?', a question avoiding 'test', a function named without backticks, a question with a decision or host word, a User: question that names a platform).
risks.mitigation: The doc comment lists these known misses, as `risks_findings` does at admission.rs:332-337. The planner brief bullet and the critic cover them. Proving a function claim true is out of scope.

risks.risk: planner.md cannot fit the new wording within the 800-token cap (at most 2397 bytes, lib.rs:408) and the unchanged facts line (same token bucket) without weakening other rules.
risks.mitigation: The edit merges overlapping wording and keeps every enumeration and pinned phrase. The producer measures with `ls -l` and runs `cargo test -p athena-context` and `cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets`. Fallbacks in order: drop ', numbered as in the brief', then '(e.g. run completed)'. If it still does not fit, the producer stops and reports that a non-deliverable change (briefs/planner.rs, or the budget figure in docs/system-facts.md) is needed. It does not drop defaults.toml, commit shapes, rule categories or the optional-doc clause. My byte counts are estimates from reading the file.

The changelog and doc comment say about 3% of newly refused plans, an estimate from the reading, not a measurement. The higher refusal rate is intended because those plans spent critic rounds on impact the planner can find by searching. A plan that keeps asking stops after MAX_MECHANICAL_PASSES (planning.rs:486), as for any major finding.

demonstrations.seam: Production entry point: `plan_findings` through the existing helper `open_question_findings_for` in the admission.rs test module (about :1190). Inputs are plain strings; no fake. Exists.

demonstrations.method: Run the full suite, plus `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus`, `cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets` and `cargo test -p athena-context`.
demonstrations.observes: Everything passes: the existing mechanical-revision tests (job_plan.rs:791 and :851, run/tests.rs:1450), `open_question_cases_get_the_expected_outcome` with the new cases, and `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` against the unchanged facts line. I read the case ids and have not seen a run.
demonstrations.fails_without: An over-broad rule would refuse an accepted case (user-decision, user-scope-question-citing-a-path, host-fact-marked-in-bold, or the admission.rs:1225-1229 list) and fail the corpus or admission tests. A planner.md size change that moves the token estimate fails `system_facts_budgets_match_computed`; a frame over 800 tokens fails lib.rs:408.
demonstrations.seam: All existing test targets; nothing is injected. The existing suite is the seam.

demonstrations.method: Read the stat and the CHANGELOG diff.
demonstrations.observes: CHANGELOG.md `## [Unreleased]` / `### Changed` has an entry for the new plan check (an open question about existing-test breakage or a named function's failure/retry path is sent back without a critic call, even with a User:/Host: prefix) and for the planner brief change. It says fake.rs was deliberately left unchanged. The files changed are planner.md, admission.rs, job_plan.rs, refusal_corpus.rs, planning.rs (comment only) and CHANGELOG.md. No records/ file, fake.rs or docs/system-facts.md changes.
